messages:
jules: Hey team — our app saw a big tail-latency spike for tenant `acme-inc` around 2026-03-17 13:20 UTC. 99.9th went from ~250ms to ~3.2s, and we saw sporadic 429s. We're on Dedicated pool `eu2-d-3` (customer-managed). Can someone check for noisy neighbor / MIG contention?

alex: Thanks Jules, I can kick this off. Do you have a sample request id or trace we can correlate?

jules: trace ids: rtx-8a7f, rtx-8a80. Both show long queues in our API gateway then timeouts to the Redwood endpoint. No config changes on our side.

alex: @priya can you pull host/GPU metrics and MIG allocation for eu2-d-3? Suspecting sibling interference.

priya: Pulling now. Quick snapshot from the node at the time (sanitized):
```
# nvidia-smi topo -m (summary)
GPU 0: MIG slices: 3 (1g.10gb x2, 2g.20gb x1)
GPU 1: MIG slices: 4 (1g.10gb x4)
...
# dcgm exporter sample: SM_UTIL GPU0=92%, GPU1=18%
# host: high PCIe bw for GPU0 at spike time
```
priya: Also saw `kubectl top` for pods on GPU0 showing one container from tenant `brightbeam` with sustained GPU utilization ~85% and continuous long sequences. Other tenants on same physical host dropped to <10% but latency for their requests jumped.

priya: Kernel logs show repeated MIG slice context switch stalls and a flurry of NVML throttling warnings around the time: "MIG slice bandwidth throttled; SM contention high".

miguel: That matches a noisy-slice pattern. Two quick hypotheses: 1) a single tenant is saturating SM and memory bandwidth causing sibling latency; 2) autoscaler/placement allowed bursty co-tenancy on same host. We should check pool placement policy and autoscaler metrics.

alex: Can we get a minimal repro to validate? Steps we can run from support side:
1) Target pool `eu2-d-3` with a synthetic client hitting `/v1/completions` using model pinned to the pool.
2) Use batch size 16, seq_len ~1024, concurrency 40 for 5m.
3) Observe GPU SM util + 99/99.9 tail latency + API 429 rate.

alex: Example stress curl (adapt before running):
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 200); do \
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \
   -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
   -d '{"model":"big-v1","input":"x" * 1000,"batch_size":16}' &\
done; wait
```

priya: I ran a controlled repro in staging targeting a node with similar MIG layout. Repro was successful: when background tenant load hit sustained >200 rps with long seqs, SM on one physical GPU saturated and sibling slices saw dramatic tail-latency increase and occasional 429s. The cluster autoscaler did not spin up more GPU nodes because the autoscaler threshold was based on pod CPU/queue length, not GPU SM utilization.

priya: Quick mitigation options:
- Move the offending tenant (`brightbeam`) to its own reserved pool or a node with isolated MIG slices.
- Adjust autoscaler to consider GPU SM% or queue latency (scale earlier).
- Apply a placement policy to avoid packing high-SM tenants on the same host.

miguel: Also longer-term: add a GPU-aware scheduler score to prefer spreading heavy infer workloads across hosts. For immediate relief we can temporarily: 1) pin `brightbeam` model to a different pool; or 2) reduce its max_concurrency / batch sizes via per-tenant rate limits.

alex: I checked billing/quotas — no throttling config at account level that would cause 429s; these 429s look like internal request rejections due to queue overflow on the node.

priya: I applied a quick placement change to prefer nodes without other heavy tenants for new `brightbeam` pods — the controller rolled new replicas to different hosts about 2m ago. Early signals: tail latency decreased from 3.2s -> ~380ms and 429s dropped. Still monitoring.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026 created: noisy-neighbor-gpu-contention-eu2-d-3. Assigned to support/alex, eng-runtime/miguel, eng-sre/priya.

jules: Great, appreciate the fast turnaround. Can you also share recommended config changes we should make to avoid this in future (per-tenant limits or preferred placement)?

miguel: We'll follow up with a short runbook: include recommended autoscaler tuning (scale on GPU util), example placement labels to prefer isolation, and suggested per-tenant rate limits. I'll drop the runbook in the ticket.

alex: Leaving next steps in the ticket: 1) monitor INC-2026 for 24h, 2) propose autoscaler change and placement policy, 3) offer tenant migration window to acme-inc if they need dedicated nodes.

jules: Thanks all :heart:

alex: Closing thread here but will update ticket with full logs and the repro script artifacts. :white_check_mark:
